sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Backend image recipe
sections.what: Builds the backend container: installs system tools and Python packages, downloads the English language model, copies in the code, and starts the API on port 8000.
sections.why: Lets the backend run the same way in every environment.
sections.watch_out: Editing the requirements file requires rebuilding the image so the new packages are installed.

summary: The recipe Docker follows to build the backend image: a Python 3.11 base, system tools, the Python packages, the spaCy English model, the app code, and the start command.
purpose: Creates a self-contained backend package that runs the same on any machine.
why: Likely reason: the backend needs specific system tools and packages, and Docker makes them repeatable.
how: Docker starts from a slim Python 3.11 image, installs gcc, the PostgreSQL client and curl, installs the packages from the requirements file, downloads the English language model for spaCy, copies the code in, creates the upload folder, opens port 8000, and starts the API server.
inputs: The backend folder, the requirements file, and the base image.
outputs: A Docker image that starts the API on port 8000.
risks: The image is large because of heavy packages such as torch. The start command has no reload setting, so code changes need a rebuild unless the compose file mounts the code.
debug: If the build fails at the package step, check the error for the package named. If the spaCy download fails, check the internet access during the build. If the API will not start, look at the container logs.
